# @ledewire/browser

> LedeWire Browser SDK — buyer authentication, checkout, wallet, and purchases for web apps.
> Works as a CDN script tag (no build step) or as an ESM npm package.
> npm install @ledewire/browser
> Source: https://github.com/ledewire/ledewire-js-sdk
> API docs: https://ledewire.github.io/ledewire-js-sdk/api/

## CDN (no install required)

```html
<!-- Pin to a major version in production -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@ledewire/browser@0/dist/ledewire.min.js"></script>
<script>
  const lw = Ledewire.init({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' })
</script>
```

The global is `Ledewire`. All methods return Promises — use async/await or `.then()`.

## npm / ESM install

```bash
npm install @ledewire/browser
```

```ts
import { init, localStorageAdapter } from '@ledewire/browser'
```

## init() configuration

```ts
import { init } from '@ledewire/browser'
import type { BrowserClientConfig } from '@ledewire/browser'

const lw = init({
  apiKey: string,           // required — your LedeWire platform API key

  baseUrl?: string,         // defaults to 'https://api.ledewire.com'

  // Token persistence — defaults to MemoryTokenStorage (cleared on page unload)
  storage?: TokenStorage,

  onTokenRefreshed?: (tokens: StoredTokens) => void,
  onAuthExpired?: () => void,  // called when refresh fails — show login UI
})
```

Token refresh is automatic — never call a refresh method manually.

## localStorageAdapter

Persist sessions across page reloads and browser restarts using `localStorage`:

```ts
import { init, localStorageAdapter } from '@ledewire/browser'

const lw = init({
  apiKey: 'your_api_key',
  storage: localStorageAdapter(),     // persists under 'lw_tokens' key
  onAuthExpired: () => showLoginModal(),
})
```

## sessionStorageAdapter

Persist sessions within the current tab only (cleared on tab close) using `sessionStorage`.
Use this to prevent token leakage across tabs — recommended for embedded checkout widgets
and kiosk-mode UIs:

```ts
import { init, sessionStorageAdapter } from '@ledewire/browser'

const lw = init({
  apiKey: 'your_api_key',
  storage: sessionStorageAdapter(),
})
```

Use `MemoryTokenStorage` (default) for highest security — tokens are never written
to disk and are cleared when the page unloads.

## Field naming convention

All API response types use `snake_case` field names (`access_token`, `price_cents`,
`content_uri`), matching the wire format exactly.

SDK-owned types use `camelCase` where they do not map 1:1 to a raw API response
field: `StoredTokens.accessToken`, `StoredTokens.expiresAt: number` (a converted
Unix ms timestamp, not the raw `expires_at: string`).

Do not attempt to remap snake_case fields — the SDK has no `transformKeys` option.

## Complete method reference

### lw.config

```ts
lw.config.getPublic() → Promise<PublicConfigResponse>
// { google_client_id: string, ... }
// Safe to call before authentication — use to get the Google Client ID for sign-in UI.
```

### lw.auth (buyer auth)

```ts
lw.auth.signup(body)                                           → Promise<AuthenticationResponse>
lw.auth.loginWithEmail({ email, password })                    → Promise<AuthenticationResponse>
lw.auth.loginWithGoogle({ id_token })                          → Promise<AuthenticationResponse>
lw.auth.loginWithBuyerApiKey({ key, secret })                  → Promise<AuthenticationResponse>
lw.auth.logout()                                               → Promise<void>
lw.auth.requestPasswordReset({ email })                        → Promise<AuthPasswordResetResponse>
lw.auth.resetPassword({ email, reset_code, password })         → Promise<AuthPasswordResetResponse>
```

Tokens are stored automatically after every successful login.
`loginWithBuyerApiKey` is useful in buyer dashboards where the user has created a
named API key and wants to authenticate headlessly (without email/password).
`signup` accepts an optional `company_invitation_token` (from a Company
invitation email) to sign up and join that Company in one step.

### lw.checkout

```ts
lw.checkout.state(contentId: string)  → Promise<CheckoutStateResponse>
```

Use this to determine what the current visitor needs to do before accessing content:

```ts
const { checkout_state } = await lw.checkout.state('article-id')

switch (checkout_state.next_required_action) {
  case 'authenticate':
    // Show login/signup UI
    break
  case 'fund_wallet':
    // Show wallet funding UI (checkout_state.has_sufficient_funds === false)
    break
  case 'purchase':
    // Show purchase confirmation UI. Single-use: has_purchased means only
    // "has ever bought" — buying (again, if needed) is how the buyer
    // receives the content, delivered directly in the purchases.create()
    // response. There is no terminal "already has access" state.
    break
}
```

### lw.wallet

```ts
lw.wallet.balance()                                    → Promise<WalletBalanceResponse>
// { balance_cents: number | null, spendable_cents: number | null, held_cents: number,
//   holds: Hold[], remaining_cents: number | null, company_name: string | null }
// balance_cents always equals spendable_cents. held_cents is committed to active
// bulk acquisitions (node-only feature); holds is one entry per such acquisition:
// { acquisition_id, held_cents, authorized_at }.
// COMPANY MEMBERS see no balance: balance_cents/spendable_cents are null,
// company_name names whose wallet pays, remaining_cents is what they may still
// spend today. content.getWithAccess().access_info.wallet_balance_cents is null
// for them too. Handle null before rendering or doing arithmetic.

lw.wallet.transactions(params?: PaginationParams)      → Promise<{ data: WalletTransactionItem[], pagination: PaginationMeta }>

lw.wallet.createPaymentSession({ amount_cents: number }) → Promise<WalletPaymentSessionResponse>
// { payment_url: string, session_id: string, ... } — redirect user to payment_url

lw.wallet.getPaymentStatus(sessionId: string)          → Promise<WalletPaymentStatusResponse>
// Poll after return from payment redirect to confirm funding.
// status: 'pending' | 'awaiting_verification' | 'processing' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'cancelled'
// completed/failed/cancelled are terminal; ACH can sit in awaiting_verification
// (microdeposits) then processing for days. Personal top-ups only.
```

### lw.purchases

```ts
lw.purchases.create({ content_id: string })           → Promise<PurchaseResponse>
lw.purchases.list(params?: PaginationParams)          → Promise<{ data: PurchaseResponse[], pagination: PaginationMeta }>
lw.purchases.get(purchaseId: string)                  → Promise<PurchaseResponse>
```

### lw.content

```ts
lw.content.getWithAccess(contentId: string) → Promise<ContentWithAccessResponse>
// Returns content payload + access info. Requires a valid buyer session.
// content_type: 'markdown' | 'html' | 'pdf' | 'image' | 'video' | 'external_ref' | 'brokered'
// content_body: plain text (SDK decodes base64 automatically) — markdown, brokered, or inline html
// content_uri: URL — external_ref, pdf, image, video, or remote html
```

### lw.user

Manage buyer API keys from a buyer-facing dashboard. Keys can be passed to
`lw.auth.loginWithBuyerApiKey()` for headless authentication.

```ts
lw.user.apiKeys.list()            → Promise<UserApiKey[]>
lw.user.apiKeys.create(body)      → Promise<UserApiKeyCreateResponse>
lw.user.apiKeys.revoke(keyId)     → Promise<void>
```

The `secret` field in the create response is shown **once** — display it
immediately in the UI and prompt the user to copy it. There is no way to retrieve
it again.

#### lw.user.spendCap

Every buyer starts with a default daily spend cap governing every wallet debit
(MCP, REST, and the web payment gate). `null` on `update()` is the only way to
become uncapped.

```ts
lw.user.spendCap.get()                                        → Promise<UserSpendCap>
lw.user.spendCap.update(body: UserSpendCapUpdateRequest)      → Promise<UserSpendCap>

interface UserSpendCap {
  cap_cents: number | null        // null once uncapped
  spent_cents: number
  remaining_cents: number | null  // null once uncapped
  resets_at: string               // ISO 8601
  spend_window_timezone: string   // IANA zone, UTC by default
  bulk_exempt: boolean
  company_name: string | null     // set for a Company member: this is their membership's cap
}

interface UserSpendCapUpdateRequest {
  daily_spend_limit_cents: number | null  // required; null removes the cap
}
```

Exceeding the cap throws `SpendCapReachedError` (402) from
`lw.purchases.create()` — funding the wallet does NOT clear it. It clears at
`resetsAt`, or when the cap is raised/removed here. A Company member's cap is
set by a Company admin (`lw.company.members.update()`); `update()` here throws
`ForbiddenError` for a member.

#### lw.user.mcpKeys

MCP API keys authenticate agent requests to the Ledewire MCP server as
`Authorization: Bearer <key>:<secret>`. Scopes are fixed at creation.

```ts
lw.user.mcpKeys.list()          → Promise<McpApiKey[]>   // secret never included
lw.user.mcpKeys.create(body)    → Promise<McpApiKeyCreateResponse>
lw.user.mcpKeys.revoke(id)      → Promise<void>

interface McpApiKeyCreateRequest {
  label: string
  can_search?: boolean            // default true
  can_purchase?: boolean          // default false
  can_manage_content?: boolean    // seller-tier — requires store_id
  can_read_analytics?: boolean    // seller-tier — requires store_id
  store_id?: string
}
```

The `secret` in the create response is shown once — store it alongside `key`.

### lw.company

A Company is a shared wallet that pays for its members' purchases; each member
spends under their own daily Spend cap and never sees the Company balance.
`membership.*` and `invitations.accept()` are for any buyer; everything else is
Company-admin only (`ForbiddenError` for a plain member, `NotFoundError` when
not in a Company). List methods return `{ data }`.

```ts
lw.company.membership.get() / .leave()
lw.company.invitations.list() / .create({ email, role? }) / .accept({ token })
lw.company.members.list() / .update(membershipId, { role?, daily_spend_limit_cents? }) / .remove(membershipId)
lw.company.machineUsers.list() / .create({ name, description? }) / .deactivate(id)   // deactivate is permanent
lw.company.machineUsers.buyerKeys.list(muId) / .create(muId, { name }) / .revoke(muId, keyId)
lw.company.machineUsers.mcpKeys.list(muId) / .create(muId, { label, scopes }) / .revoke(muId, keyId)
lw.company.wallet.createPaymentSession({ amount_cents, currency }) / .listPendingTopUps()
lw.company.purchases.list({ member?, from?, to?, kind?, page?, per_page? })   // paginated
lw.company.spend.list({ member?, from?, to? })
```

`members.*` take the membership id (`CompanyMember.id`), not `user_id`. Key
`secret`s from `machineUsers.*Keys.create()` are shown once. A Company top-up
is not found by `lw.wallet.getPaymentStatus()` — track it with
`listPendingTopUps()`, where it drops off once settled.

### lw.seller

Operations scoped to the authenticated seller's store.
Store identity is derived server-side from the token — no `store_id` needed.

```ts
// Authenticate first (key-only → view; key + secret → full)
lw.seller.loginWithApiKey({ key, secret? })           → Promise<AuthenticationResponse>
// key-only → view permission (read-only, sufficient for lw.seller.content.*)
// key + secret → full permission (read/write)

// 1. Obtain a view token (key-only is sufficient)
await lw.seller.loginWithApiKey({ key: 'your_api_key' })

// 2. List all store content
lw.seller.content.list()                              → Promise<ContentResponse[]>

// 3. Search by title, URI, or metadata (AND logic — at least one field required)
lw.seller.content.search({ title?: string, uri?: string, metadata?: Record<string, unknown> })
                                                      → Promise<ContentResponse[]>

// 4. Fetch a single item
lw.seller.content.get(contentId: string)              → Promise<ContentResponse>
```

## Full checkout flow example

Purchases are single-use: `has_purchased` means only "has ever bought", and a
past purchase does not by itself grant access again. Buying is how the buyer
receives the content — delivered directly in the `purchases.create()` response,
which is the only place `content_body` / `content_uri` appear for a purchase.
That delivery is one-time — persist it immediately; there is no route that
serves the same content a second time.

```ts
const lw = Ledewire.init({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' })

const { checkout_state } = await lw.checkout.state('article-123')

switch (checkout_state.next_required_action) {
  case 'authenticate':
    await lw.auth.loginWithEmail({ email, password })
    break

  case 'fund_wallet':
    const session = await lw.wallet.createPaymentSession({ amount_cents: 500 })
    window.location.href = session.payment_url  // Stripe checkout
    break

  case 'purchase': {
    const purchase = await lw.purchases.create({ content_id: 'article-123' })
    await saveDeliveredContent(purchase) // persist now — one-time delivery

    // content_body is always plain UTF-8 on the wire, never base64-encoded.
    // What it contains depends on purchase.content.content_type.
    if (purchase.content_body && purchase.content.content_type === 'markdown') {
      renderMarkdown(purchase.content_body)
    } else if (purchase.content_body && purchase.content.content_type === 'html') {
      // Inline HTML is seller-supplied — sanitise before inserting it.
      container.innerHTML = DOMPurify.sanitize(purchase.content_body)
    } else if (purchase.content_uri) {
      // Seller-supplied URI — check the scheme before navigating to it.
      const uri = new URL(purchase.content_uri)
      if (['https:', 'http:'].includes(uri.protocol)) {
        window.location.href = purchase.content_uri  // redirect to gated video/PDF
      }
    }
    break
  }
}
```

## Google OAuth sign-in setup

```ts
// Fetch the platform's Google Client ID before the user signs in:
const { google_client_id } = await lw.config.getPublic()
google.accounts.id.initialize({
  client_id: google_client_id,
  callback: async ({ credential }) => {
    await lw.auth.loginWithGoogle({ id_token: credential })
  },
})
google.accounts.id.renderButton(document.getElementById('signin-btn'), { theme: 'outline' })
```

## Key types

```ts
interface CheckoutStateResponse {
  content_id: string
  content_title: string
  price_cents: number
  checkout_state: {
    is_authenticated: boolean
    has_sufficient_funds: boolean | null  // null when not authenticated
    has_purchased: boolean
    next_required_action: 'authenticate' | 'fund_wallet' | 'purchase'
  }
}

interface StoredTokens {
  accessToken: string
  refreshToken: string
  expiresAt: number  // Unix timestamp (ms)
}

interface TokenStorage {
  getTokens(): Promise<StoredTokens | null>
  setTokens(tokens: StoredTokens): Promise<void>
  clearTokens(): Promise<void>
}
```

## Error classes

All errors extend `LedewireError`. Import named subclasses for actionable handling:

```ts
import {
  LedewireError,
  AuthError,
  ForbiddenError,
  NotFoundError,
  PurchaseError,
  SpendCapReachedError,
} from '@ledewire/browser'

class LedewireError extends Error {
  statusCode: number        // HTTP status code
  code: number | undefined  // machine-readable code from API body
  message: string           // human-readable description from API body
  type: ErrorTypeValue | undefined  // machine-readable error.type, e.g. 'daily_spend_cap_reached'
  details: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined  // extra top-level error-body fields
}

class AuthError extends LedewireError {}       // 401 — bad credentials / session expired
class ForbiddenError extends LedewireError {}  // 403 — authenticated but access denied
class NotFoundError extends LedewireError {}   // 404 — resource not found
class PurchaseError extends LedewireError {}   // 409/422 — purchase validation failure

// 402 — daily_spend_cap_reached, thrown by lw.purchases.create(). Funding the
// wallet does NOT clear this — it resets at `resetsAt`, or via
// lw.user.spendCap.update().
class SpendCapReachedError extends LedewireError {
  capCents: number
  spentCents: number
  remainingCents: number
  resetsAt: string    // ISO 8601
  bulkExempt: boolean
}
```

`instanceof` checks work even across the separately bundled copies of
`@ledewire/core` inside `@ledewire/browser`, `@ledewire/node`, and
`@ledewire/x402-client`.

```ts
try {
  await lw.purchases.create({ content_id: 'article-123' })
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof SpendCapReachedError) {
    // A daily policy limit — do NOT prompt the buyer to fund their wallet.
    showError(`Spend cap reached. Resets at ${err.resetsAt}.`)
  } else if (err instanceof AuthError) {
    showLoginModal()
  } else if (err instanceof PurchaseError) {
    showError('Purchase failed: ' + err.message)
  }
}
```
